chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say about eating the irbiyan?' He said to me, 'There is no harm in that, and the irbiyan is a type of fish.' I said, 'Some of your mawali have narrated regarding eating the rabitha.' He said, 'There is no harm.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And it is disliked to hunt wild animals and birds at night.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating irbiyan and rabitha fish in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that 'irbiyan' and 'rabitha' are specific varieties of fish, thereby confirming their permissibility (halal) for consumption, which resolves potential confusion regarding their classification. The text concludes with a juristic note from Shaykh al-Tusi distinguishing this permissibility from the general dislike (makruh) of hunting wild game and birds at night, highlighting the nuanced approach to different types of seafood and game in Shia fiqh.
